1  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. OF 2023  (arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.1486 of 2022)
 NOMA M.C. FERNANDES ..... 
 VERSUS  UNION TERRITORY OF DIU-DAMAN & ANR. ..... R  O R D E R Leave granted.
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties at some length, we are of the opinion that the registration of the First Information Report bearing C.R. No. 6/2016 dated 11.01.2016, registered with Nani Daman Police Station, under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 17 of the Indian Citizenship Act, 1955 in the present case is unwanted and unnecessary.

It is an accepted position that the appellant - Noma M.C. Fernandes was an Indian citizen when she was appointed as a Lower Division Clerk (LDC) on 09.01.2012 in the Electricity Department, U.T.
Administration of Daman & Diu.
During the course of employment, the appellant - Noma M.C. Fernandes acquired a Portuguese passport, which was issued on 26.02.2015.
Date: 2023.06.16 Thereupon, she had informed the Regional Passport 16:08:27 IST

Reason:
Officer, Mumbai and filed an application for cancellation of her Indian passport on 27.03.2015.
Her Indian passport was cancelled on 07.04.2015.

sentences.text: M.C. Fernandes had also moved an application for cancellation of her Ration Card on 31.03.2015.
On 01.04.2015, the appellant  Noma M.C. Fernandes had submitted her resignation from the post of LDC, Electricity Department, U.T. Administration of Daman & Diu.

We find it rather strange that the authorities have not accepted her application for resignation and,
in fact, the Secretary (Power)/Development Commissioner, Daman, on 02.05.2015, called for a report on the appellant - Noma M.C. Fernandes from the police and also referred the matter to the Superintendent of Police, Daman.
One of the allegations made in the counter affidavit is that the appellant - Noma M.C. Fernandes,
while applying for the Portuguese passport had stated that she was unemployed.
It is to be noted that this application was not made to any Indian authority, and the Portuguese authorities are not aggrieved by the said mis- description/statement.
We fail to understand how the offences under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and/or Section 17 of the Indian Citizenship Act, 1955 are made out.

Accordingly, we quash the proceedings arising out of the First Information Report bearing C.R. No.
6/2016 dated 11.01.2016, registered with Nani Daman Police Station, against the appellant - Noma M.C. Fernandes.
Recording the aforesaid, the appeal is allowed in the above terms without any order as to costs.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
..................J. (SANJIV KHANNA) ..................

J. (M.M. SUNDRESH) NEW DELHI;
MAY 19, 2023.
